name: Story First, Calm
description: The story arrives before anything else asks the viewer for something. An unheaded invitation, the episode itself, then the housekeeping — credits, a closing line, hashtags — kept quiet and last. This is the shape a calm narration channel already uses.
architecture: Unheaded invitation, then the episode, then quiet housekeeping last.

sections.instruction: Write one unhurried paragraph that invites the viewer to settle in and begin listening. Speak to a person who is already tired and is choosing what to fall asleep to. Do not summarise the episode here and do not mention the channel.

Describe what this episode contains, in the same unhurried voice, as a continuation of the paragraph above rather than a separate blurb. Name the places, the movement and the mood. Do not use the phrase tonight we will or any variation of a presenter introducing a segment.
List the narration and soundscape credits, one per line, plainly. If a credit is unknown, leave that line out rather than inventing one.
Write one short closing line wishing the listener rest. One sentence, no exclamation marks, no request to subscribe.
Emit only hashtags, on a single line, separated by spaces. No sentence, no heading, no commentary.

title_plan.guidance: Calm and concrete. Name the place and the journey. No hype words, no question marks, no capitalised shouting.

tag_plan.guidance: for this calm long-form narration episode, mixing the setting, the mood and the listening occasion

constraints: Never address the viewer as guys, folks, or friends.
No exclamation marks anywhere in the description.
Ask for nothing until the closing line, and even there ask gently.
